newsitem.title: PERU: Andean miners dug raid tunnels, two died-report.
newsitem.headline: Andean miners dug raid tunnels, two died-report.

text.p: Miners from Peru's Andes were recruited to dig the tunnels used to launch a rescue operation on the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima and two of them died in the process, a local newspaper reported on Friday.

The miners, from the state company Centromin Peru, started working on the tunnels in late January, the report in pro-government Expreso said. Officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
Two miners were buried alive when one of the tunnels collapsed, the paper added, citing unnamed Centromin sources.
The tunnels were apparently built under the cover of loud martial music blasted at the residence by police.

President Alberto Fujimori detailed on Wednesday a warren of at least five tunnels that criss-crossed the property and allowed troops to burst in on Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages as they played indoor soccer.

The commandos spent more than a day waiting in the tunnels before the order for Tuesday's raid. One of the hostages, two army officers and all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas were killed in the attack that ended the 126-day standoff.
